correctness.rationale: For every fixed radius 0<r<1 and every real smooth h, the Poisson operator sends the boundary Taylor series to a C² expansion. Expanding the nonvanishing circle derivative yields an exact second variation; the first coefficient integrates to zero, and Parseval gives πr Σ_{k≠0}(1−d_k²)|h_k|². Strict C² convexity preserves equality of arclength and convex-hull perimeter. For k≥3, the proof maximizes the explicit scalar t^{(k−3)/2}|(k+1)t−(k−1)|/2 and proves |d_k|<r. Thus k=1 and k=2 alone determine the exact sharp gap, and their squared magnitudes cross only at r=1/3. The standalone checker was executed successfully with 762 supplementary assertions; finite checks are not substitutes for the proof.

value.rationale: A natural quantitative refinement of a sharp 2026 harmonic mean-width/perimeter inequality: explicit all-frequency second-variation coefficients, a sharp L² gap modulo rotations, complete equality modes and a nontrivial exact frequency transition at radius 1/3. This is a structural feature of the harmonic Poisson operator that neither follows from the global inequality nor represents an arbitrary numerical slice. The result creates a precise local benchmark for potential nonlinear stability theorems without claiming them.
